title: Tooling: exact modular rank fast path for historical joint-frame verification
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This contribution adds an opt-in verification package under
`research/joint-frame-modular-screen/` for the historical
`scripts/audit_joint_frames.py` certificate.

The adapter uses exact elimination modulo 101 to certify full rational
rank. If the modular reduction is rank-deficient, or a denominator is
divisible by 101, it falls back to the unchanged original rational
elimination routine. No approximate rank decision is used.

The supplied benchmark records a reduction in median complete-certificate
wall time from 1.952577 s to 1.701918 s (12.8% lower) across seven
alternating fresh-process A/B pairs. All fourteen timed certificates
are byte-identical. One individual pair was slower; the timing result
is specific to the recorded environment, not a universal speedup claim.

This is a tooling improvement, not a new construction or conditional
bound. No improved kappa or practical integer-multiplication speedup
is claimed.

## Provenance and scope

- Exact investigation base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`
- Assignment track: verification engineering
- OS-random assignment seed: 85
- `SOURCE.json` records SHA-256 and Git-blob pins for 36 predecessor inputs.
- `CLAIM.json` records task selection, the local claim, and overlap checks.
- `NOTICE.md` credits predecessor and related concurrent work.

The supplied patch adds only this research package and leaves existing
scripts, default verification commands, the selected frontier, and
`upstream/` unchanged.

## Validation

The supplied verification record reports:

- All 2,644 actual uncached rank calls agree individually with the
  original rational routine: 752 modular full-rank certificates and
  1,892 exact fallbacks.
- 12 focused test groups, including an independent determinant/minor
  oracle over 530 binary matrices and 240 seed-85 rational matrices.
- Four deliberately incorrect kernels detected by counterexamples.
- All eight unchanged historical tests pass with both engines.
- All fourteen timed complete certificates match exactly.
- Source-drift controls and rejection of disabled assertions.
- Successful `make selected-record-check` and staged whitespace checks.

Reproduce from the repository root using Python 3.11+ on Linux or macOS,
with a fresh output path:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/joint-frame-modular-screen/verify.py --pairs 7 --output /tmp/joint-frame-rank-result.json
```

Expected final marker:

```text
PASS_JOINT_FRAME_MODULAR_SCREEN
```

Expected historical certificate SHA-256:

```text
b7686b518e4e677ca5e6f92066a41255bd696abae6c7b0c4f09d11eb6e8bdffd
```

`PROOF.md` supplies the algebraic equivalence argument for the fast path.
The finite test campaign and certificate replays are not a formal proof
of the full multiplication theorem.

## Limitations and checks not performed

This package targets the historical joint-frame audit, not the selected
supplier reconstruction. It does not reopen the closed fixed-boundary
search or resolve the inherited obligations of the selected theorem.

Full repository `make verify`, selected cold reconstruction, Lean builds,
and hosted CI were not run during preparation and are not claimed here.

The recorded overlap review was performed at
2026-10-13T05:15:10.714617Z; it is not a claim about subsequent PRs.

## Attribution and AI assistance

Prepared at Martin Rivera's request with substantial OpenAI Codex
assistance, as disclosed in the supplied `NOTICE.md`. The AI assistant
implemented the optimization, wrote the argument and tests, recorded
the measurements, and prepared the handoff.

No independent human review or official OpenAI endorsement is claimed.
The contribution is provided under Apache-2.0.
